article.title: Making a Killing
article.author: Pat Hynes
article.content: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Antonio Guterres, in his last attendance as secretary-general of the UN, told the UN Conference on Climate Change (COP31) gathered in Antalya, Turkey in November that he “ will not stop telling the truth ” about how the fossil fuel industry and wealthy governments are handing out oil and gas subsidies, all to enjoy massive profits, while people globally suffer from the climate emergency. They make a killing while killing the planet, he said…assuring “mutually assured destruction.” Oil and gas and coal need a catastrophe like the dinosaurs, rendering them extinct. The illegal war in Iran, launched by the U.S. and Israel, has brought in billions of windfall profits to oil and gas companies while the UN’s Loss and Damage Fund, dedicated to funding climate-related damages in developing countries, languishes with millions rather than billions of needed funds. In its report to the COP 31, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) warned that the last 12 years have been the world’s warmest, but the last 4 years have seen warming accelerate. Recent polling reveals that, even in wealthy countries, a majority of citizens agree with taxing gas and oil profits aggressively, and they support a strong transition away from fossil fuels. However, many of their presidents, prime ministers, and chancellors skipped the summit – a sign of their fealty to the fossil fuel industry over their citizens. Related: My Peace Shrine While the summit took place behind closed doors; the People’s Climate Summit rallied to one simple message: “climate justice now.” Translated it means: climate finance to countries in need in “grants not just promises;” “ reparations for harm already done ;” “a just, fair transition away from fossil fuels.” But financing costs for developing countries is estimated to rise to $420 billion by 2035, which “will still achieve only 20% to 29% of what is needed” for those countries to handle disastrous climate impacts. Panama, negotiating as a member of a Latin American coalition of developing countries, threatened to block any final agreement that does not initiate a transition away from fossil fuels. “ Beautiful speeches won’t save the planet ,” said the country’s Environment Minister Jan Carlos Navarro, calling the pressure from fossil fuel companies “corrupt behavior…blocking every single step of these processes.” On November 23, the COP31 ended, having run 2 days overtime. It was deemed a “ colossal failure .” The conference conclusion made no reference to fossil fuels and no reference to eliminating or transitioning from them. The largest climate polluter, the United States ignored the conference; and Saudi Arabia and Russia worked against the mention of fossil fuels. They and countries like them are killing our future. The world is doomed to overshoot the temperature we must stay below, 1.5 degrees Centigrade, if we are to have a livable world. And the blame rests squarely on the shoulders of rich polluting countries and the fossil fuel industries they support. The final report did not admit the root cause of the climate crisis; it failed to augment climate finance for developing countries and ignored the legal obligations of those countries that have caused harm to prevent and repair the harm to vulnerable countries. “ This has been the worst ever COP and its collapse needs to be a wake-up call for the world ,” Mohamed Adow director of the think tank Power Shift Africa said, sizing up the conference in which rich nations arrived “empty-handed,” hoping a carefully worded but empty declaration would “get them off the hook.” Savio Corvalho of 350.org summed up the situation: …”After a year of devastating wildfires, floods and collapsing glaciers,” you would think that “world leaders would finally rise to the moment. But they didn’t: no clear plan to exit oil, gas and coal; no money to aid the survival of countries devastated by climate breakdown.“ We will keep pushing until governments end the age of fossil fuels,” he said resolutely. Related: Coral Reefs: “Rainforests of the Sea” A “ Planetary Health Check 2026 ,” authored by more than 60 scientists and produced by the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research has found that seven of nine breached boundaries of Earth’s life support systems continue to worsen. “Potentially irreversible change is increasing” as record droughts and land heat, ocean heat, floods and wildfires increasingly burden the Earth systems and its people. Planetary emergencies have hit Pakistan, Europe, the Caribbean, Nepal, Canada and the coral reefs. “This is a peace process” – peace with the Earth – “the whole world must commit to, together, starting now,” said the co-Vice Chair of the Planetary Health Check, 2026. If not, the fossil fuel industry and its vassal states will destroy us.
